key_insight: D-Gun-sprayed NiCrAlY delivered greater hardness and corrosion resistance on Al 6061-T6, while 80Ni20Cr showed better solid-particle erosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: Coating selection should match the dominant damage mechanism: NiCrAlY for hardness and chloride-corrosion protection, or 80Ni20Cr for the tested erosion exposure.
method: Deposit 80Ni20Cr and NiCrAlY coatings on Al 6061-T6 using detonation gun spraying.
Characterise microstructure, phases, roughness and hardness using SEM-EDS, XRD, AFM and nanoindentation.
Evaluate corrosion in 3.5 wt% NaCl, wettability and solid-particle erosion.
evidence_signal: NiCrAlY reached 7895.36 MPa hardness versus 780.11 MPa for 80Ni20Cr, with corrosion rates of 0.00567 versus 0.01427 mm/year; 80Ni20Cr had the lowest erosion mass loss.
watch_item: Results reflect laboratory corrosion testing and one erosion condition (90° impact, 40 m/s, 5 min), not long-term service-life performance.
paper_title: Microstructure and surface performance of detonation gun sprayed 80Ni20Cr and NiCrAlY coatings on Al 6061-T6 substrate for structural applications
